video_caption: The video opens with a screen displaying a digital audio workstation interface, featuring bold white text with black outlines that reads "SKRILLEX VOCAL CHOP CHORDS" (SKRILLEX VOCAL CHOP CHORDS), indicating the content will demonstrate how to create Skrillex-style vocal chop chords. Music with a distinctive chopped vocal sample plays in the background. At 0:10, the scene transitions to a man with dark hair tied back, wearing round glasses and a black hoodie with "ODYSSEY" printed on it in colorful, retro-style font. He is seated in what appears to be a home studio, with a white keyboard or MIDI controller on a wooden desk and white shelves in the background. The man speaks enthusiastically to the camera, using hand gestures and smiling, as an overlaid text briefly appears, asking "Is such a thing even possible?" (Is such a thing even possible?). From 0:16, the interface of the music production plugin "Serum" is digitally superimposed over his right shoulder as he explains its capabilities, stating it "literally does everything" from bases to leads, pads, and drums. The video then transitions at 0:28 to a screen capture of the Splice website, showing the "Xfer Records Serum" plugin page with a futuristic graphic of a piano keyboard and a wavy green line. The page displays details such as "RENT-TO-OWN $9.99/mo. for 19 months" and a description: "Luscious pads. Beastly bases. Lion-toothed leads. Find your future sound in the critically-acclaimed wavetable synthesizer." (Luscious pads. Beastly bases. Lion-toothed leads. Find your future sound in the critically-acclaimed wavetable synthesizer.). The video quickly cuts back to the man, who continues to advocate for Serum, with the text overlay "**not even sponsored**" (not even sponsored) appearing over his chest, emphasizing his genuine recommendation.

The video begins with a man, sporting dark hair tied back, glasses with pinkish frames, and a black "ODYSSEY" hoodie, smiling and gesturing with his right hand in what appears to be a home music studio, featuring a keyboard, microwave, and shelves in the background. This scene quickly transitions to an animated title card with the white text "FB2B" against a vibrant purple and pink gradient background, accompanied by upbeat electronic music. The video then cuts back to the man, now sitting in front of a computer screen displaying a Digital Audio Workstation (DAW) interface, likely Ableton Live, with numerous colored audio tracks and waveforms. As he speaks, a white text overlay appears on the screen, stating "1. Find Acapella" (This indicates the first step in his process). He explains, "I normally use my own vocals but for demonstration purposes I'm using an acapella from a sample pack," gesturing towards the screen where an audio clip labeled "Cymatics - Let You Go - Lead Vocal Dry" is highlighted, and a short vocal snippet of the acapella plays.

A man with dark hair tied in a bun, wearing glasses and a black hoodie with "ODYSSEY" printed on it, is featured in a home studio setting, speaking to the camera about music production techniques. He sits in front of a keyboard/MIDI controller, with shelves containing a toaster and plants in the background. Initially, text overlays his speech, stating: "i like to transpose to a certain key" (English: "I like to transpose to a certain key"). He explains his process of transposing an audio sample in Ableton Live to a specific key, then adjusts the "Transpose" dial in the software from -2 semitones to 10 semitones. A text overlay briefly appears: "hotkey = SHIFT+up arrow to transpose by octave". He emphasizes that transposing by exactly 12 semitones (one octave, as another text overlay clarifies: "1 octave is 12 semitones") would result in an undesirable "chipmunk vocal." A brief audio clip of a high-pitched vocal demonstrates this "chipmunk" effect. He then explains that at 10 semitones, he achieves a "nice, happy medium." The video then highlights the Ableton Live interface, with a text overlay instructing: "set Warp Mode to COMPLEX PRO to access the formants bar," demonstrating how to manipulate the "Formants" control to further refine the vocal sound, showing the formant value changing from 57.03 to 81.25 and 75.78, accompanied by corresponding audio changes.

The video opens with a man in a black "ODYSSEY" hoodie and round glasses, with his hair tied back in a bun, looking intently at a computer screen displaying a digital audio workstation (DAW) with multiple audio tracks. He uses a mouse to select a red audio waveform segment, and text appears on screen saying, "i'll just pick random spots." He then listens to a short audio clip, and the text changes to "hit the space bar." He continues to select and play various short segments, which are highlighted in red, yellow, and green. The camera then cuts to a closer shot of the man, where he is explaining his process, gesticulating with his hands. Text overlays this shot: "look for vocals w/ transients and syllables." The scene returns to the DAW screen, where he repeats the process of selecting and playing different vocal samples, which are shown as distinct waveform segments in various colors. In the background, a music keyboard, speakers, and shelves with books and plants are visible.

In a home studio setting, a man with his dark hair tied back and wearing glasses and a black "ODYSSEY IV" hoodie is seen sitting at a desk, engaging with a digital audio workstation (DAW) on his computer screen. The DAW interface displays various audio tracks with pink/red and blue waveforms. Initially, the man highlights small segments of a pink/red vocal track, demonstrating "wobbly notes" that are not suitable for chopping. An overlaid text appears, stating, "this is important because the quality of your chops affect everything" to emphasize the selection process. He then highlights another unsuitable segment, described as having "wonky timing." Subsequently, the text overlay changes to "3. Assemble Vocal Chops into a melody/pattern," as the man demonstrates how he arranges selected vocal chops into a repetitive melody or pattern across multiple tracks in the DAW. Throughout the segment, he looks between the screen and the camera, occasionally gesturing with his right hand while explaining the process. In the background, a white keyboard and other studio equipment are visible.

A man with dark hair tied in a bun, wearing round glasses and a black hoodie with "ODYSSEY" in pink and purple letters, speaks directly to the camera, using hand gestures. He is seated in front of a computer screen, with a MIDI keyboard and a microphone visible on a desk to his left, and white shelves in the background. The video then transitions to a screen recording of music production software, Ableton Live, where the man appears in a small window at the bottom right. A white text overlay appears on the screen, reading "4. Make a chord progression," as he explains the next step in music production. The software interface changes to a synthesizer plugin called Serum; a close-up focuses on the "OSC A" (Oscillator A) section with another text overlay indicating to "set wavetable position to here -> (saw wave)," referring to adjusting the waveform to a saw wave. He returns to speaking about making a chord progression in G major, gesturing with his hands to emphasize points. Another text overlay flashes, stating "needs to complement," highlighting that the chord progression must support the existing vocal element. The screen then shows the Ableton Live timeline with multiple tracks: a red track containing audio waveforms labeled "Cyma," and blue tracks below it containing MIDI notes labeled "Em9" and "drone." The audio plays, and the MIDI notes are highlighted as they scroll past, demonstrating the vocal chop with the complementary chord progression and drone.

The video segment features a man with dark hair tied in a bun, wearing glasses and a black hoodie with a colorful "ODYSSEY" logo, seated in what appears to be a home studio with a MIDI keyboard and microphone on his desk. He is demonstrating music production techniques using a digital audio workstation (DAW) displayed on his computer screen. From 0:03, the screen shows blue blocks representing musical chords, labeled with names like "Em9", "Cmaj9", "Am7", and "Bm9", which the man identifies as the chords he used. At 0:08, an on-screen text overlay reads "use 7th and 9th chords", clarifying his chord choice. The view then shifts back to the DAW showing red audio waveforms and blue MIDI notes, with the man explaining the rhythm. At 0:11, he instructs the viewer to rename a track to "Carrier", which is highlighted on screen with an accompanying text overlay: "rename the track 'Carrier'". He then clicks a button to deactivate it, with text appearing: "deactivate the track". Following this, the man makes a surprised and confused expression, placing his hands on his head and exclaiming, "Get rid of it. What? Why on earth would I do that?" before smiling at the camera and saying, "Chill, we're gonna get...". The background includes shelves with various items, including a toaster, suggesting a casual, possibly kitchen-adjacent, home office setup.

In the segment, a young man with dark hair tied back, wearing glasses and a black hoodie with the word "ODYSSEY" written across the chest in pink and blue, speaks directly to the camera. He gestures with his hands and smiles, appearing enthusiastic. He is in what looks like a home studio or living space, with a keyboard in the foreground and shelves holding various items, including a toaster oven and storage boxes, in the background. Around the 00:05 mark, the video transitions to a screen recording of a digital audio workstation (DAW) interface, likely Ableton Live, showing audio waveforms and MIDI tracks labeled "Em9" and "drone" as a mouse cursor moves across them.

The video opens with a dark, wide shot of a concert audience, illuminated by stage lights and the glowing screens of mobile phones held aloft, showing people moving rhythmically to music. The scene then transitions indoors to a well-lit room where a man with dark hair, glasses, and a black hoodie with "ODYSSEY" printed on it is speaking directly to the camera. He gestures expressively with his hands, making a fist and looking upwards as he talks, with a keyboard, microphone, and shelves visible in the background. An inset picture briefly appears in the lower-left corner, showing a young man with light blue hair. The main speaker points his finger, then makes a fist, before the word "VOCODER" appears in large white text on the screen. The video concludes by showing a screen recording of a digital audio workstation (DAW) interface, specifically highlighting a "Vocoder" plugin with its various controls and a visualizer displaying moving blue frequency bars, implying an active audio effect.

In a split-screen view, a man with dark hair tied in a bun, wearing glasses and a black "ODYSSEY" hoodie, sits at a desk with a keyboard, interacting with a music production software (Ableton Live). He looks at the screen on the left, explaining how a "beautiful vocal chop" is created using three main components: a Vocoder, an OTT (Over The Top compressor), and an Auto Pan, all visible as plugins in the software's Audio Effect Rack at the bottom of the screen. He demonstrates setting the Vocoder's "Carrier" to "External" and selecting "Carrier" from the "Audio From" dropdown menu, which is highlighted from a long list of tracks including "vocals," "drone," and various instrument and FX tracks. A text overlay appears saying, "that's why we named the serum track 'Carrier'." He then explains the process: running a Serum synthesizer track (named "Carrier") through the Vocoder, which processes it and adds harmonics to the vocal based on the chord progression from the Serum track. The screen briefly shows the Serum plugin interface. He then activates the vocoder effect, causing a visual representation of frequency bands to light up in the Vocoder plugin. He turns the "Dry/Wet" knob on the Vocoder to 100%, smiling and nodding with satisfaction, as the processed vocal sound plays. The main Ableton Live window shows audio waveforms (red for vocals, blue for chords/drones) and MIDI clips.

The video opens with a man, wearing a black hoodie and glasses, with his long dark hair tied in a bun, sitting in front of a computer screen displaying music production software (Ableton Live). He gestures with his hands as he explains a technique using the "OTT" audio plugin. A close-up on the software shows the "Vocoder" and "OTT" plugins, where he adjusts the "Dry/Wet" knob on the Vocoder from 100% down to around 55%, demonstrating how it balances the original vocal chop with harmonics. He then explains, with a text overlay "OTT brings out harmonics hiding in your sound," that using OTT helps get a more accurate sound. He toggles the "OTT" plugin on and off to showcase its effect, with the input levels changing significantly when active. The scene then transitions to a humorous segment: the man, now wearing a light green t-shirt, glasses, and a novelty headband with flashing red and blue police lights, animatedly pretends to call the "producer police" on his phone, looking surprised and then smiling. This is followed by a quick shot of another man, wearing a police hat, aviator sunglasses, and a mustache, with an animated hand holding a lemon near his mouth, saying "Somebody called? What's going on here?" The scene cuts back to the man in the light green t-shirt, still on the phone, pointing and gesturing emphatically, with the flashing police lights on his head, stating that the first man is "just copying other sounds and he doesn't want anybody to become unique producers." The video concludes with the man in the black hoodie and glasses back in his studio setting, looking directly at the camera with a slight smile and saying "said no one."

In this video segment, a man with his dark hair in a top knot and wearing round glasses and a black "ODYSSEY" hoodie addresses the viewer directly from a brightly lit room. He gestures with his hands as he explains a concept related to sound production. Behind him, a piano keyboard, white shelving units, a television, and framed artwork are visible. At 0:19, text appears on the screen, stating, "keep watching and I'll show how to modify this sound & make it UNIQUE to YOU" (Keep watching and I'll show how to modify this sound and make it unique to you), followed by the man giving a thumbs-up. The video then transitions to a screen recording of music production software (Ableton Live), where a "Vocoder" plugin is displayed. The man's voiceover guides the viewer through adjusting settings like the number of bands (set to 20), range (12.0 kHz), and a visual EQ graph, demonstrating how to cut out mid-frequencies. He reappears briefly on screen to explain the reasoning behind these adjustments, then the view returns to the software, showing the "Vocoder" and "OTT" plugins as he tweaks settings, demonstrating the vocal chop and vocoder harmonies with audio playback. Finally, the video shifts to a picture-in-picture format at 0:51, with the man visible in a smaller frame while the main screen displays the Ableton Live software. He enables and adjusts an "Auto Pan" plugin, explaining its function in creating movement in the sound, with the audio demonstrating the panning effect.

A man with long dark hair tied in a bun, wearing glasses and a black hoodie with "ODYSSEY" printed on it, is featured demonstrating music production techniques using Ableton Live software. He smiles and gestures while explaining how to use the "Auto Pan" plugin. The video shows close-ups of the Ableton Live interface, highlighting the "Auto Pan" plugin's settings, including Amount, Rate, Phase, Shape, and Offset. Automation lanes are visible, and he specifically demonstrates automating the "Auto Pan Sync Rate" to "1/8th" (0:07, text overlay: "Automate RATE to 1/8th") and occasionally to "1/16th" for accentuation (0:16, text overlay: "just as an accent"). He then shows automating the "Auto Pan Amount," setting it around "81.8%" to balance the effect's strength, and at times reducing it to "0.00%" to let longer notes breathe. The man concludes by emphasizing the trial and error process of finding the right balance for the desired wavy sound, while the background reveals a home studio setup with a MIDI keyboard and shelves.

The video features a man with dark hair tied back, wearing glasses and a black hoodie with "ODYSSEY" printed in colorful letters, demonstrating music production in Ableton Live. He navigates the software, showcasing various audio tracks and effects like Vocoder, OTT, Auto Pan, EQ Eight, and Reverb, as he builds a musical track. He adds a drum beat, with the screen zooming in to highlight the "Drum Rack" and specific samples such as "Cymatics - Dry Snare," "REMEDY KICK 23," and "REMEDY SNARE 11." As the full track, including an 808 bassline, plays, the man smiles, bobs his head, and gestures enthusiastically. The scene then transitions to a close-up of him, where he makes a "ta-da" gesture, gives a thumbs-up, and, while holding a white mug, explains that he will show how to customize the sound. The video concludes with him returning to the Ableton Live interface, opening the "Serum" synthesizer plugin to demonstrate further sound manipulation.

The video features a man with dark hair in a bun, wearing glasses and a black hoodie with "ODYSSEY" printed on it, demonstrating music production techniques in Ableton Live. He is initially shown interacting with the Serum VST plugin, enabling and adjusting 'Phaser' and 'Hyper / Dimension' effects, which distinctly alter the synthesized vocal sound. The video then transitions to a full-screen shot of the man addressing the camera, emphasizing that a vocoder works best with a simple and clean carrier sound, a point reinforced by overlaid text: "Vocoder works best when the Carrier sound is simple / clean". A small inset video shows a man with a man bun and glasses in a light green t-shirt. He then returns to the Ableton Live interface, where he actively manipulates the 'Formant', 'Dry/Wet', and 'Depth' knobs within the Vocoder effect, each adjustment dramatically changing the tone, blend, and presence of the vocoded vocal sound. Finally, he opens the audio clip view of the original vocal sample and adjusts its 'Formants' parameter, demonstrating another way to manipulate the sound, before stating that all these parameters can be automated. The background shows a home studio setup with a MIDI keyboard, headphones, a toaster, and white shelving units.

The video opens with a man with dark, shoulder-length hair tied back, wearing glasses and a black hoodie with "ODYSSEY" in colorful, stylized text. He is smiling and talking directly to the camera, seated in what appears to be a home studio setup with a keyboard/MIDI controller, computer monitor, keyboard, and mouse visible on a desk in front of him. In the background, there's a kitchen counter with appliances to the left and a white shelving unit with decorative items to the right. From 0:03 to 0:07, a white YouTube interface overlay appears over his chest, showing a heart icon, "SUBSCRIBE", and a bell icon. A cursor animation clicks "SUBSCRIBE", which changes to "SUBSCRIBED", and then clicks the bell, causing it to animate as if ringing. At 0:13, white text on a black oval overlay appears over his chest, reading "@ashfb2b" (a social media handle, likely for Instagram or Twitter, encouraging viewers to follow him). He briefly closes his eyes and smiles before looking back at the camera. From 0:20 to 0:23, the word "FREE!" (meaning the project file is free) appears in bold white text with a black outline over his forehead. He then makes a gesture to the right side of the screen, and the scene abruptly transitions at 0:29 to a vibrant, neon-pink and purple overlay of a digital audio workstation (DAW) interface, likely Ableton Live. Overlaid on this glowing screen, in white text, are the messages: "thanks for watching!!" (a thank you to the viewer), "if you like what i'm doing" (a conditional statement), "pls like and subscribe" (a call to action for engagement), and once again, "@ashfb2b" (his social media handle). The DAW interface continues to display for the remainder of the segment.
